title: Abaris’s arrow and Jesus taken up in glory
source_text: Εἰ δὲ ταῦθ᾿ οὕτως ἔχει, πῶς οὐκ εὔλογον μὲν νομίζειν περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τοσαῦτα συστῆσαι δεδυνημένου, ὅτι οὐχ ἡ τυχοῦσα θειότης ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, οὐκέτι δὲ οὔτε ἐν τῷ Προκοννησίῳ Ἀριστέᾳ. κἂν ὁ Ἀπόλλων αὐτὸν βούληται ἐν θεῶν μοίρᾳ νέμειν, οὔτ᾿ ἐν οἷς ἐξαριθμεῖται ὁ Κέλσος λέγων ὅτι οὐδεὶς νομίζει θεὸν Ἄβαριν τὸν Ὑπερβόρειον, ὃς δύναμιν εἶχε τοσήνδε, ὥστε ὀϊστῷ [βέλει] συμφέρεσθαι; τί γὰρ βουλομένη ἡ χαρισαμένη θειότης τῷ Ὑπερβορείῳ Ἀβάριδι ὀϊστῷ συμφέρεσθαι τὸ τηλικοῦτον αὐτῷ ἐδωρεῖτο: ἵνα τι ὠφεληθῇ τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος; ἢ αὐτὸς ἐκεῖνος τί ὤνατο ὀϊστῷ συμφέρεσθαι; ἵνα καὶ συγχωρηθῇ ταῦτα μηδαμῶς εἶναι πλάσματα ἀλλὰ κατά τινα δαιμονίου συνεργίαν γεγονέναι. ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ἐμὸς Ἰησοῦς ἀναλαμβάνεσθαι „ἐν δόξῃ“ λέγηται, ὁρῶ τὴν οἰκονομίαν, ὅτι τοῖς θεωρήσασι συνίστη τὸν διδάσκαλον ὁ τοῦτ᾿ ἐνεργήσας γενέσθαι θεός· ἵν᾿ ὡς οὐχ ὑπὲρ ἀνθρωπίνων μαθημάτων ἀλλὰ θείας διδασκαλίας ἀγωνιζόμενοι ὅση δύναμις ἑαυτοὺς ἀναθῶσι τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ καὶ πάντα πράττωσιν ὑπὲρ τῆς πρὸς ἐκεῖνον ἀρεσκείας, ὡς ἀποληψόμενοι κατ᾿ ἀξίαν ἐν θείῳ δικαστηρίῳ ἅπερ ἐν τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ εὖ ἢ κακῶς πεποιήκασιν.
pass_a_gloss: But if these things are so, how [is it] not reasonable (εὔλογος) to think about Jesus, having been able (δύναμαι) to establish (συνίστημι) so many things, that not the ordinary/chance (ἡ τυχοῦσα) divinity (θειότης) was in him, but no longer [so] either in Aristeas of Proconnesus, even if Apollo wish to assign (νέμω) him in the lot/rank of gods (ἐν θεῶν μοίρᾳ), nor in those whom Celsus enumerates (ἐξαριθμέομαι) saying: no one thinks (νομίζω) Abaris the Hyperborean a god, who had (ἔχω) such power (δύναμις) as to be carried along with (συμφέρομαι) an arrow (ὀϊστός) [gloss βέλει bracketed]? For wishing what (τί βουλομένη) did the divinity that granted (χαρίζομαι) to the Hyperborean Abaris to be carried with an arrow bestow (δωρέομαι) so great a thing on him: that the race of men (τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος) be benefited (ὠφελέω) somewhat? Or what did he himself profit (ὀνίνημι) to be carried with an arrow? — even if it be granted (συγχωρέω) these things to be by no means fictions (πλάσματα) but to have happened by some cooperation (συνεργία) of a demon/divine being (δαιμόνιον). But if my Jesus be said to be taken up (ἀναλαμβάνομαι) ‘in glory’ (ἐν δόξῃ), I see the dispensation/plan (οἰκονομία), that to those who beheld (θεωρέω) the God who worked (ἐνεργέω) this to happen commended (συνίστημι) the teacher; in order that as contending (ἀγωνίζομαι) not for human lessons (μαθήματα) but for divine teaching (διδασκαλία), as much as [their] power, they might dedicate (ἀνατίθημι) themselves to the God over all and do (πράττω) all things for the pleasing (ἀρέσκεια) toward him, as about to receive back (ἀπολαμβάνω) according to worth (κατ᾿ ἀξίαν) at a divine tribunal (δικαστήριον) what in this life (βίος) they have done well or badly.
pass_b_english: If this is so, is it not reasonable to think of Jesus, who has been able to establish so much, that no ordinary divinity was in him, but no longer reasonable to think so of Aristeas of Proconnesus, even if Apollo wishes to assign him a place among the gods, nor of those whom Celsus lists when he says, “No one thinks Abaris the Hyperborean a god, who had such power that he was carried along on an arrow”? For with what purpose did the divinity that let Abaris the Hyperborean be carried along on an arrow bestow so great a gift on him? So that the human race might be helped in some way? Or what did he himself gain by being carried along on an arrow? And this is even granting that these things are by no means fictions but came about through the cooperation of some demon.

But if my Jesus is said to have been taken up “in glory” (1 Timothy 3:16), I see the plan in it: the God who brought this about was commending the teacher to those who saw it, so that, as men contending not for human teachings but for divine teaching, they might devote themselves with all their strength to the God over all and do everything to please him, as those who would receive at the divine judgment seat, according to their deserts, whatever they had done in this life, whether good or evil (compare 2 Corinthians 5:10).

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 31 (Koetschau 3.31). Celsus’s sentence about Abaris (οὐδεὶς νομίζει θεὸν Ἄβαριν …) follows ‘λέγων ὅτι’ with a finite verb and is set in quotation marks as his own words; the Aristeas clause is Origen’s summary of Celsus (see 3.26–29) and is unquoted. The staged text brackets ‘[βέλει]’ after ὀϊστῷ as an editorial deletion (a gloss on ‘arrow’); not translated. ‘συμφέρεσθαι’ rendered ‘carried along on’: Celsus’s wording means travelling with or upon the arrow (the older legend has Abaris carrying an arrow round the earth, Herodotus 4.36; not cited inline because Origen quotes Celsus, not Herodotus). The opening question is long in the Greek: ‘that no ordinary divinity was in him, but no longer (οὐκέτι δέ) in Aristeas … nor (οὔτ᾿) in those whom Celsus lists’; the negatives are kept: Origen denies such divinity to Aristeas and Abaris. ‘δαιμονίου συνεργίαν’ rendered ‘the cooperation of some demon’, in line with this translation’s use of ‘demon’ for Origen’s δαίμων/δαιμόνιον. ‘ἀναλαμβάνεσθαι ἐν δόξῃ’ quotes 1 Timothy 3:16 (ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ). The last clause (ἀποληψόμενοι κατ᾿ ἀξίαν … ἅπερ … εὖ ἢ κακῶς πεποιήκασιν) is a clear allusion to 2 Corinthians 5:10 (ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος … εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε φαῦλον); ‘whether good or evil’ renders ‘εὖ ἢ κακῶς’ (well or ill). ‘ὅση δύναμις’ rendered ‘with all their strength’ (as far as they are able). ‘as men contending’ renders ὡς with the participle. The μέν/οὐκέτι δέ contrast hangs on ‘εὔλογον’, so the English repeats ‘reasonable’ (‘but no longer reasonable to think so of Aristeas’).
Checked the staged row against the Perseus TEI (3.31): complete
Aristeas clause: ‘while this is no longer so of Aristeas’ made ‘but no longer reasonable to think so of Aristeas’, so the μέν/οὐκέτι δέ contrast on εὔλογον is clear
Calque ‘granted Hyperborean Abaris to be carried’ made ‘let Abaris the Hyperborean be carried’
Removed added ‘knowing that’ (ὡς + participle = ‘as men contending’)
Checked 1 Timothy 3:16 (ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ) and 2 Corinthians 5:10 (whether good or bad); both fit
